newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian blue chips slide in high turnover.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian blue chips slide in high turnover.

text.p: Large volumes of leading Nigerian shares changed hands on Tuesday and some manufacturing stocks ended the day weaker, taking the stock market lower, traders said.
Because of technical problems, the all-share index could not be updated.
Traders said leading manufacturing stocks finished weaker. "The continuing lower profitability of some of these blue chips remains a source of worry for investors," one trader said.

Lever Brothers fell 20 kobo to 20.20 naira after it announced lower profits on Monday. Cadbury also closed 20 kobo lower at 21.50 naira, the same as tyre maker Dunlop which ended at 8.00 naira, its lowest price this year.
Conglomerate UAC and pharmaceutical group Smithkline Beecham, whose nine-month results on Tuesday showed net profits still below those of comparable 1995 periods, were unchanged.
West African Portland Cement Company ended 10 kobo stronger at 46.15 naira on traders' positive perception. "Its low price earnings ratio makes it an attractive stock," one dealer said.
But other cement shares were on the slide. Ashaka Cement fell 10 kobo to 16.80 naira while Benue Cement lost two kobo at 7.28 naira.
Oil shares made small gains. Unipetrol rose 20 kobo to 58.25 naira, National Oil added 15 kobo to 46.95 naira and Total went 10 kobo up to 57.40 naira.
Banks traded mixed as United Bank for Africa closed at 6.00 naira, 10 kobo higher, while Guaranty Trust Bank slumped by the same margin to 11.30 naira.
Only Guinness advanced in the brewing sector, closing five kobo stronger at 8.15 naira.
